Rocca d'Anfo, Italy -- More in Comments

Rocca d'Anfo is a fortified complex originally constructed by the Venetian Republic in 1450 to guard their border with the state of Trento. After surviving attacks by both the Holy Roman Empire and the Austrian Habsburgs in the 1500s it eventually fell to the Napoleonic Army in 1796. From 1813 to 1814 the complex was the site of an intense siege by Austrian troops. Napoleon's soldiers held but Rocca d'Anfo and the surrounding holdings were surrendered to the Austrian Empire in a peace treaty. The area saw many skirmishes in following years between the northern Italian states and Austria. It was later Incorporated into the Kingdom of Italy in 1915. The complex continued to be used as a training area and ammunition storage by the Italian army until 1975.
